HDI concerns easing
New capacity and price hikes boosting earnings visibility for 2027-28
We are increasingly confident in Gold Circuit’s transition towards higher-layer-
count HDI boards, supported by meaningful investments in technology, talent, and
new capacity. The planned capacity ramp aligns well with the next-generation

ASIC schedules of two major CSP customers, while potential layer-count increase
from 26 layers for Trainium3 to 34 layers for Trainium4 should drive meaningful
content growth. Meanwhile, PCB price hikes and improving cost pass-through
should support a sequential GM recovery from 3Q26. We raise our 2027/28 EPS
forecasts by 1%/9% and lift our TP from NT$1,955 to NT$2,000 while reiterating
our High Conviction Outperform rating.
Less concerned about the HDI transition

While the market remains concerned about Gold Circuit’s HDI capabilities, we
believe the company has recruited experienced talent and invested meaningfully in
HDI technology to support future ASIC demand. The second Thailand plant and
new capacity at the first Suzhou plant are scheduled to contribute from 2H27,
followed by the second Suzhou plant in 1H28, with all three expansions primarily
dedicated to HDI production. Importantly, the capacity ramp should align well with

the next-generation ASIC schedules of two major CSP customers. We expect Gold
Circuit to maintain its leading position in AWS Trainium4 and benefit from
meaningful content growth, driven by an increase in PCB layer count from 26 layers
for Trainium3 to 34 layers for Trainium4.
Price hikes underway
For AI accelerator PCBs, we believe Gold Circuit should gradually pass rising CCL
costs through to customers. Our checks suggest that non-AI PCB products are

being quoted at 3-4x prior price levels, with lead-times extending to at least four
months at leading PCB vendors. This indicates a tightening industry supply-demand
environment and suggests that the GM weakness seen in 2Q26 should not persist
in the coming quarters. We forecast GM to improve sequentially to 36.7%/36.8%
in 3Q26/4Q26.
Earnings revisions and valuation
We keep 2026SP EPS largely unchanged but raise our 2027/28 forecasts by 1%/9%
to reflect higher production value contributed by the new plants and increasing HDI

content. Accordingly, we raise our TP from NT$1,955 to NT$2,000, still based on
30x 2H27-1H28SP PE, and reiterate our High Conviction Outperform rating.

Investment thesis
We expect Gold Circuit to benefit from the strong CCL/PCB material upgrade trend,
rising shipments of AI servers and continued spec upgrades in CPU servers, which
require higher PCB layer counts. The upgrade in networking towards 800G should
also lead to improving margins for the company.
Catalysts
1) Accelerating server shipments driven by US CSPs and enterprise customers; 2)

server content value growth; 3) a stronger-than-expected networking demand
recovery; 4) a notebook demand recovery.
Valuation details
We value all of our coverage in the PCB/CCL space on PE as it better reflects
margins and earnings outlooks, which we believe the market will mainly focus on.
We use a target PE multiple of 30x, in line with the downstream server sector
average after the recent rerating driven by AI. Given GCE's higher-than-peer
revenue exposure to cloud servers and switches, its leading market position, and

our expectation of robust AI/ASIC server shipments with computing server demand
to gradually recover, we think 30x PE is justified as server/PC ODM suppliers have
all rerated to the 15-30x range on the back of the booming AI demand. And as GCE
also generates a similar number of sales from server and AI, it will likely enjoy strong
growth (better content growth from server and switch) and better returns (less
competition) than assemblers in the mid-to-long term.

Investment risks
Downside risks: (1) order adjustment as a result of chip shortages or supply chain
disruption; (2) weaker-than-expected cloud/datacentre Capex demand; (3) slower
adoption or delayed launch of Intel’s Eagle Stream and AMD’s Genoa platforms; (4)
further raw material price hikes, and (5) more severe competition across the
industry.

個股報告 
資料來源：CMoney；兆豐投顧預估

營 運 分 析

台達電為全球電源管理及散熱解決方案領導廠商 
台達電(2308)成立於 1971 年並於 1988 年掛牌上市，成立初期分別投入生產
交換式電源供應器與無碳刷式直流風扇，目 前已取得全球電源產品龍頭地
位。2017 年公司啟動組織調整，以「電源及零組件」、「自動化」、「基礎
設施」、「交通」四大業務範疇，並從傳統關鍵零組件製造商逐步轉型為節
能解決方案提供者。近年隨AI 資料中心建置需求爆發，公司積極將既有電源
技術延伸至 AI伺服器電源機櫃、液冷 side car、BBU、DC-DC/AC-DC模組
及 CDU 等新產品線，目前終端應用已從傳統 NB/工業電源、資料中心跨足
至高壓供電(HVDC)與液冷散熱系統，客戶涵蓋NVIDIA與北美 CSP及 ASIC
供應鏈。

26Q2 營收比重:(1)電源及零組件 53%,包含電源、被動元件等零組件、風扇
散熱;(2)交通 5%,電動車解決方案;(3)自動化 8%,包含工業自動化,樓宇自動
化;(4)基礎設施 34%,包含資訊通訊技術(通信電源、網通交換器、資料中心
解決方案、液冷side car)、能源基礎設施(電動車充電樁、可再生能源及儲能
設備等)。受惠 AI 資料中心電源需求與規格持續提升，台達持續擴充台灣、
中國大陸、泰國與美國產能，並同步推進 800V HVDC 架構開發，全面迎接
NVIDIA 新世代 GPU 機櫃功耗大幅提升所帶動的電源與散熱升級需求。

台達電(2308)公告 8月營收：營收 645.9 億元，MoM -3.7%/YoY +34.9%，
Q3達成率 62.4%，低於研究部預期與市場共識，係因 MOSFET 全產品線呈
現缺料所致，故研究部下修台達電 26Q3 營收 1960.8 億元(原估 2,107.4 億
元)，QoQ +7.0%/YoY +30.4%，而先前 18.3KW PSU 因電容問題有進行產
品召回，不過預期本月將處理完畢且對財務無任何影響；毛利率方面，受惠
產品組合轉佳與規模經濟抵銷原料/電子元件漲價影響，預估毛利率 35.8%，
仍可維持與上季相當，季增 0.2ppt，反映營收下修，同步下修稅後淨利 232.6
億元，QoQ -7.5%/YoY +25.0%，EPS 9元(原估 10.5 元)。

AI 電源與散熱產品持續放量，輔以新產品推出，2026 EPS 37元 
展望 2026 年，主要成長動能仍來自 AI 資料中心電源、散熱與基礎設施，在
電源方面隨著 GB300 持續放量與 H2 VR200之 18.3KW 產品開始出貨，預
期價量齊揚挹注營運動能，此外 HVDC(±400V/800V)產品於 3Q26 開始量
產，惟在初期階段預期僅小幅貢獻；在散熱產品方面(涵蓋水冷板、Manifold、
CDU及 Sidecar)在 2026 下半年可望延續成長動能，主要受惠液冷滲透率持
續提升與內容價值同步墊高。綜上所述，反映 Q3下修，同步下修台達電 2026
年營運預估：2026 年營收 7,465.4 億元，YoY +34.5%，毛利率 36.2%，年
增 1.9ppt，稅後淨利 960.8 億元，YoY +59.8%，EPS 37.0元（原估 40 元）。

展望 2027 年，受惠 CSP業者 CAPEX 持續增長，公司為滿足訂單需求，持
續加大投資力道，2026 年資本支出約 700 億元(YoY +50%)，資金來源除自
有資金外，9/15 公告發行泰達電可交換公司債籌措 15 億美元以滿足擴產資
金需求，2027 年也可望維持高檔水準，預計於泰國、中國、台灣與美國同步
擴產，研究部認為 HVDC(±400V/800V)較大規模量產貢獻有望於 2027 年起
顯現，同時液冷、電源機櫃、DC-DC模組等新產品線持續放量，此外公司亦
持續推進 SST 與 SOFC 等能源基礎設施長期布局，電源產業將迎來新格局

1 群益投顧 
ASML (ASML US) 與台積電 (2330 TT) 共同推動 High NA EUV 將自現行的 6 吋光罩，
轉移至更大的 12 吋 光 罩。 目標於 2031 年之前建立 12 吋 光 罩 試 產 線(pilot line) ， 並 於
2033 年之前實現微影系統全面就緒。台積電並表示自 2030 年 起 ， 將 在 先 進 製 程 量 產
中導入 ASML 的 High NA  EUV 。台積電與 ASML 共同發起 6 吋光罩轉移至 12 吋光
罩 的 規 格 轉 移 ， 其 戰 略 意 義 在 於 ， 製 訂 規 格 和 標 準 ， 確 保 台 積 電 技 術 領 先 地 位 。 因 此
對 台 積 電 的 投 資 評 等 Buy ，目標價 3,200 元。

研 究 員 ： 陳 俐 妍   
ly.c@capital.com.tw

ASML 與 台 積 電 共 同 推 動 High NA EUV 將 自 現 行 的 6 吋 光 罩 ， 轉 移 至 更 大
的 12 吋 光 罩 ：  
09/07/2026 ASML 與 台 積 電 於 BACUS 國 際 光 學 工 程 學 會(SPIE) 先 進 微 影 技
術 研 討 會 前 宣 布 發 起 產 業 合 作 ， 共 同 推 動High NA EUV 將 自 現 行 的 6 吋光
罩 ， 轉 移 至 更 大 的 12 吋 光 罩 ， 預 期 將 進 一 步 提 升 晶 圓 廠 的 生 產 力 、 降 低 晶
片 製 造 成 本 ， 並 消 除 需 要 2 張 6 吋 光 罩 在 High NA EUV 曝 光 時 進 行 拼 接 的
限 制，使 整 個 半 導 體 產 業 受 惠。此 轉 移 能 讓 先 進 晶 片 製 造 服 務 提 供 者 充 分 利
用 High NA EUV 的 優 勢 ， 更 提 升 未 來 世 代 先 進 晶 片 的 成 本 效 益 。 
目標於 2031 年 之 前 建 立 12 吋 光 罩 試 產 線(pilot line) ，並於 2033 年 之 前 實
現 微 影 系 統 全 面 就 緒 ， 以 支 援 先 進 製 程 量 產 。 台 積 電 並 表 示 自2030 年 起 ，
將 在 先 進 製 程 量 產 中 導 入 ASML 的 High NA 技 術 。  
12 吋光罩 使 High NA 效 率 提 升 ：  
現行 EUV 設備的 NA(Numerical Aperture ， NA) 為 0.33 ， High NA 則 提 高 到
0.55 。 NA 數 值 越 高 ， 解 析 度 也 越 高 、 曝 光 時 能 呈 現 的 細 節 愈 多 。ASML 資
料顯示 High NA 可 將 最 小 解 析 尺 寸 從 現 行 EUV 的約 13 奈 米 進 一 步 縮 小 到
8 奈 米 ， 也 就 是 能 在 晶 圓 上 印 出 更 細 微 的 電 路 圖 形 。 部 分 原 本 需 要2 次 甚 至
更多次曝光才能完成的圖形，也有機會改以單次曝光處理，降低製程複雜
度 、 缺 陷 風 險 與 生 產 周 期 。 
舉 例 來 說 ，0.33 NA EUV 機 台 ， 至 少 需 要 4 張 光 罩 、 分 多 次 曝 光 才 能 完 成
A14 、 A10 金 屬 層 圖 形 ；High NA EUV ， 只 要 1 張 光 罩 就 能 完 成 相 同 圖 形 。
但 解 析 度 提 高 ，High NA 的 光 學 設 計 讓 單 次 可 曝 光 範 圍 縮 小 到 原 本EUV 的
50% ， 製 作 大 顆 晶 片 時 可 能 必 須 分 成2 次 曝 光 ， 再 把 圖 形 拼 接 起 來 。 這 也 是
台積電與 ASML 此 次 推 動 12 吋 光 罩 的 原 因 ， 相 較 現 行 6 吋 光 罩 ， 放 大 光 罩
尺 寸 預 期 能 進 一 步 提 升 晶 圓 廠 生 產 力、降 低 晶 片 製 造 成 本，並 消 除 High NA
曝 光 時 的 拼 接 限 制 。 
台 積 電 預 計 2030 年 開 始 使 用 High NA  EUV ， 推估 High NA 將 會 在 A10 或
A10 以 下 的 先 進 製 程 採 用：  
台積電預計 2030 年 開 始 導入 High NA  EUV ，比 12 吋 光 罩 微 影 系 統 預 計 全
面就緒的 2033 年 更 早 。 這 代 表 台 積 電 初 期 導 入High NA 時 ， 仍 會 先 使 用 現
行 6 吋 光 罩 ， 之 後 再 隨 12 吋 光 罩 與 相 關 系 統 成 熟 逐 步 轉 換 。

2 群益投顧 
根 據 台 積 電 目 前 公 開 的 製 程 藍 圖 ，A13 與 A12 製 程 都 預 計 2029 年 量 產 。 其
中 A13 是 A14 平 台 的 延 伸 ，A12 則 將 超 級 電 軌(Super Power Rail) 背面供電
技術導入 A14 平 台 。 因 此 N2 、 A16 、 A14 、 A13 與 A12 都 早 於 台 積 電 預 計
2030 年 導 入 High NA ， 推 估 High NA 將 會 在 A10 或 A10 以 下 的 先 進 製 程 採
用。  
Intel (INTC US) 和 Samsung (005930 KS) 領 先 台 積 電 採 用 High NA EUV ，但
也 同 時 參 與 12 吋 光 罩 開 發 ：  
Intel 在 2024 年 宣 布 完 成 全 球 首 套 商 用 High NA EUV 設 備 的 組 裝 ；2026 年
High NA 已 經 正 式 進 入 量 產 ， 並 用 於 部 分 18A 製 程 層 。 是 目 前 High NA 導
入 進 度 最 快 的 晶 片 製 造 商 。Samsung 則預計 2028 年導入 DRAM 量 產 ； 台 積
電選擇在 2030 年 導 入 。Intel 和 Samsung 也 同 時 表 示 與 ASML 及 供 應 鏈 合
作 ， 推 動 未 來 轉 向 大 尺 寸 光 罩 。 
台 積 電 與 ASML 共 同 發 起 6 吋 光 罩 轉 移 至 12 吋 光 罩 的 規 格 轉 移，將 領 導 業
界 規 格 ：  
6 吋 光 罩 轉 移 至 12 吋光罩 的 這 項 升 級 非 單 純 的 尺 寸 放 大 ， 而 是 面 臨 生 態 系
與 物 理 極 限 的 多 重 挑 戰 。 整 體 供 應 鏈 重 構 ， 包 括 基 板 與 材 料 以 及 設 備 等 等 。
12 吋 光 罩 石 英 基 板 的 平 坦 度 、 缺 陷 密 度 與 熱 膨 脹 係 數 控 制 難 度 倍 增 。 製 程
設 備 如 薄 膜 沉 積、蝕 刻、清 洗 與 自 動 化 搬 運 設 備 皆 需 重 新 開 發。後 續 檢 測 與
量測極限檢測難度也增加，更大面積的圖形缺陷檢測（ Inspection ）與修補
技 術 需 要 突 破 。 在 12 吋 面 積 上 維 持 奈 米 級 的 對 位 精 度 與 線 寬 均 勻 性 極 為 困
難   
電 子 設 計 自 動 化 (EDA) 工 具 必 須 重 新 適 應 大 尺 寸 曝 光 視 場 與 資 料 處 理 。 12 
吋 光 罩 的 圖 形 檔 案 與 運 算 複 雜 度 將 大 幅 上 升 。 
台積電與 ASML 共 同 發 起 6 吋 光 罩 轉 移 至 12 吋 光 罩 的 規 格 轉 移，其 戰略意
義在於 ，台 積 電 為 全 球 最 大 晶 圓 代 工 廠，為 先 進 製 程 最 大 的 供 應 商，可 以 領
導 光 罩 基 底 供 應 商 、 光 罩 檢 測 設 備 商， 甚 至 EDA 廠 等 整 個 生 態 系 ，除 共同
分攤 ， 跨 越 升 級 12 吋 光 罩 的 龐 大 研 發 成 本外 ， 製 訂 規 格 和 標 準 ， 確 保 台 積
電 技 術 領 先 地 位 。因 此 對 台 積 電 的投 資 評 等 Buy ， 目 標 價 3,200 元。

貳、公 司 概 況 
一.公司簡介  
截至 2026 年 5 月（法說資料），裕民實際經營船隻為 71 艘：  
海岬型船   25 艘：自有 22 艘 + 3 艘合資。  
巴拿馬型船 24 艘：自有 14 艘 + 7 艘代管  + 3 艘合資 。 
輕便型      8 艘（自有） 。 
水泥船      4 艘（自有） 。 
油輪        4 艘：透過  環能海運 （持股 40% ）。 
CTV 離岸風電人員運輸船 6 艘（自有  ； 裕民風能航運 ）。

在建船隻  12 艘，交船時程 ： 
202 6 年： 輕便型  1 艘（預期 11 月交付）。 
202 7 年 及 2028 年： 
海岬型  4 艘 + 輕便型  5 艘 + 風電工程船  2 艘。

二.營運概況 及展望  
1.超級聖嬰 造成缺水  撞上  巴拿馬運河乾季，壓抑海運供給  
2026 年 5 月，全球進入聖嬰年，加劇全球乾旱與極端高溫 的
氣候異常 。 聯合國  世界氣象組織（ WMO ）表示， 這波聖嬰
現象，可能是過去  40 年最強一次，幾乎肯定會持續到  2027
年 2 月，很可能打破  2023 年 ~ 2024 年的紀錄 。

巴拿馬運河溝通大西洋與太平洋，節省海運船舶至少  3,000
海哩的航程，航行時間縮短  2 週左右。

但由於 大西洋與太平洋的海平面和水流高度不同，船隻 要透
過 巴 拿 馬 運 河 ，橫 跨 美 洲 ， 必 須依 靠 巴 拿 馬 運 河 的船閘 注
水，採取類似 爬樓梯一樣 的升降 動作 ，讓船 隻從海平面被提
升到高處的加通湖，穿過湖面後，再降回另一側的海平面。
每艘船舶 每次通過船閘，都需要消耗  加通湖  數以百萬加侖
計算的淡水。

因此， 加通湖的水量多寡 ，會影響巴拿馬運河的運作效率與
容量 ，一旦缺水，巴拿馬運河每日通行船舶數量就會減少。

觀察過去 5 年（2021 年 ~ 2025 年）加通湖的水位資料（參閱
圖 1） ，通常會從每年 5 月，逐月爬升到  12 月；  但 2026 年
超級聖嬰的乾旱，造成目前 9 月水位不升反降 。

Yageo
Valuation
We set our target price at NT$1,450, based on 35x average 2027E-28E earnings. We value Yageo based on PE as we believe the
company’s earnings performance and industry dynamics would be the key focuses of the market. Our target multiple of 35x is
at the higher end of the trading range since 2022. During this period the company has gone through the cycles, successfully
integrated the acquired business to enhance its product offerings, and started to deliver stable margins and earnings.

Risks
Key downside risks to our target price and rating include: 1) slower-than-expected demand recovery; 2) intensified peer and
pricing competition; 3) execution risks associated with M&A integration and synergies; and 4) FX and interest rate fluctuations.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

### Page 1

1. Photonics IC scaling up: AI drives data transmission speed and bandwidth 
requirement, leading to strong demand on Photonics IC, requesting it to catch up 
Electrical IC automated production and testing ecosystem in 1 to 2 years, while EIC / 
semiconductors has been developed for decades. The strong demand brings 
opportunities to tool suppliers, across coupling and testing, which are necessary 
tools to accelerate PIC production. Robotechnik / FiconTEC describes the numbers of 
tools they target to ship in coming 1 year would be over 50% of what they’ve shipped 
in past 25 years, reflecting the strong demand and orders visibility.  
2. Testing - CPO earliest beneficiary: As a new technology, CPO naturally takes time 
and faces challenges in the path of commercialization; however, we identify testing 
equipment suppliers as the earliest beneficiaries, considering the expensive final 
module means multiple testing during the production process is necessary, given the 
earlier a failure is found, the lower cost a failure is. As a result, companies we visited 
continue to see Insertion 2 (double sided wafer-level testing) as necessary, and 
Robotechnik / FiconTEC launched the new generation in 3Q26, which fully complied 
with the global leading foundry’s communication infrastructure. 
3. Testing - shortening time with KGD (know good die) at early stage: To facilitate 
photonics IC scaling up, not only are more tools needed but better tools, requiring 
suppliers’ strong R&D and execution, delivering continuous specification upgrade. 
Robotechnik / FiconTEC, as global leaders in PIC testing, aim to shorten the 
wafer-level testing time by 50-60% next year, and target 4x faster die-level testing 
next year. Enlitech (7728.TWO, Not Covered) offers NightJar, a hyperspectral image 
system, revealing AWG (arrayed waveguide grating) optical loss pathways with 
absolute optical power mapping, allowing customers to KGD at Insertion 1 (PIC wafer

### Page 2

testing) or Insertion 0 (PIC wafer early defect screening), saving failure costs. 
4. Coupling - automated production becoming necessary in high-speed connection: 
AI drives optical module towards high speed and high density / bandwidth, driving 
demand on automated production. GMT (4573.TWO, Not Covered) showcased dual FA 
active alignment equipment for 1.6T optical module, which could do the coupling for 
both Tx and Rx simultaneously, saving 50% of coupling time compared to traditional 
equipment. FitTech (6706.TW, Not Covered) showcased optical engine assembly system, 
featuring with passive / active alignment and customized development of coupling 
algorithms, which could be used in multiple products: high-speed optical modules, ELS, 
OCS, NPO, CPO, SiPh and optical chiplets. ASMPT showcased MEGA multi-chip bonding 
solution for complex multi-chip and photonics packaging applications, combining 
high-precision placement with adhesive dispensing, UV fixation and 3D inspection in one 
platform. 
5. FAU & Laser specification upgrade: With optical networking expanding from scale 
out to scale up, FAU and laser specification is also migrating. We estimate FOCI‘s FAU in 
2026E to be mainly 40 channels (starting in 3Q26) for 3.2T, followed by 80 channels 
(within 2026E) for 6.4T, and 100 channels under R&D. The company’s FAU enjoys several 
customers across fabless, foundry, laser suppliers, etc. FOCI Aug revenues accelerated to 
+20% MoM (vs. +9% MoM in Jul), reflecting the ramp up of high-end FAU. VPEC‘s 
optoelectronics revenues enjoy strong growth on the back of strong CW lasers demand 
and InP substrate supply getting better. Its InP epiwafer for CW lasers is also migrating 
from 70mW / 100mW (scale out) to above 100mW (scale up, NPO) and 300mW / 
400mW (scale up, CPO), along with expansion from CW lasers to 100G / 200G EML, 
supporting its growth ahead. 
6. AI drives CMP slurry: Anji Micro owns a comprehensive customer base, allowing it to 
ride on growing AI spending across China and overseas. The global-tier AI infrastructure 
continues to migrate, driving the CMP slurry consumption per system, along with AI 
server racks ramp up, enlarging the total addressable market. As the CMP slurry local 
leader, we are positive on Anji’s capability to offer qualified and reliable semi material 
products to penetrate global-tier clients.   
Company highlights

Robotechnik (300757.SZ, Buy, 12m TP at Rmb796) Chairman & Head of FiconTest 
visit: We hosted Robotechnik Chairman and Head of FiconTest and visited the booth in 
Semicon Taiwan on Sep 3. Management of Robotechnik highlights the strong demand on 
Photonics IC automated production and testing, driving their tools demand. The 
company’s strong beat in 2Q26 results (report link) reaffirms our positive view on 
Robotechnik, riding on the growing trend across CPO, NPO, OCS, and optical modules. 
We identify Robotechnik to be the major beneficiary in the photonics IC scaling trend, 
considering its comprehensive tools coverage and strong automation capability across 
software and hardware. Read more: Robotechnik / FiconTEC Semicon Taiwan 
takeaways.  
VPEC (2455.TW, Buy, 12m TP at NT$793), Chairman visit: We hosted VPEC Chairman 
and CFO in Semicon Taiwan on Sep 3. Management remains positive on their

optoelectronics business, riding on the AI infrastructure cycle, specification upgrades,

Enlitech (7728.TWO, Not Covered), Chairman visit: We hosted Enlitech Chairman,

Taiwan on Sep 3. Management remains positive on their CPO FAU business and expects
strong earnings growth ahead, riding on AI server racks ramp up and FAU specification
upgrade (from 40 channels to 100 channels). FOCI’s FAU started shipment in 3Q26,
driving Aug revenues growth accelerating to +20% MoM (vs. +9% MoM in July). We
expect CPO FAU revenue growth to further accelerate in 2H27, driving CPO FAU revenue

contribution up to 58% / 73% in 2027 / 28E (vs. 21% in 2026E), supporting GM
expansion to 37.9% by 2028E (vs. 18.8% in 2025A). Read more: FOCI Semicon Taiwan
takeaways.
GMT (4573.TWO, Not Covered): We visited GMT booth in Semicon Taiwan on Sep 3.
GMT showcased four launched system covering wafer-level optical inspection and
testing, as well as optical-engine active alignment for 1.6T optical modules. The
company highlighted automation and simultaneous TX/RX coupling, saving coupling

time by 50% compared to traditional methodology. Read more: GMT Semicon Taiwan
takeaways.
Fittech (6706.TW, Not Covered): We visited Fittech booth in Semicon Taiwan on Sep 3.
The company showcased equipment solutions for lens and FAU inspection,
high-precision optical coupling and bonding, PIC chip testing, etc. Management expects
FitTech to ride on the rising optical networking device end demand in AIDC and
specification upgrade towards 1.6T, 3.2T, CPO, NPO, driving the company’s growth

ahead. Read more: Fittech Semicon Taiwan takeaways.
Anji Micro (688019.SS, Buy, 12m TP at Rmb509): We visited Anji Micro booth in
Semicon Taiwan on Sep 3. The company demonstrated products incl. CMP Slurry, Post
CMP Cleaner etc. during the event. Key discussions focused on (1) CMP Slurry product
upgrade, (2) semi client demand, and (3) diversified customer base. Overall,
management is positive on the rising capex spending from both memory and advanced

logic clients, along with the specification upgrade towards high-end products. Read
more: Anji Micro Semicon Taiwan takeaways.
ASMPT (0522.HK, Neutral, 12m TP at HK$177): We visited ASMPT booth in Semicon

Price target methodology and risks - ASMPT
Valuation methodology: We are Neutral-rated on ASMPT with a 12-month target price
of HK$177, which is based on 24.9x 2030E discounted P/E (discounted back to 2027E).
Our target P/E is derived from correlation between peers P/E to the sum of NI YoY and
OPM.
Key upside/downside risks: 1) customers’ faster-/slower-than-expected adoption of
Advanced Packaging tools; 2) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand from

automotive customers; and 3) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand for traditional
IC packaging and SMT equipment.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - Anji Micro
Valuation: We are Buy-rated on Anji Micro with a 12-month target price of Rmb509,
which is based on 46x 2030E discounted P/E (discounted back to 2027E). Our target P/E
is derived from correlation between peers P/E to the sum of NI YoY and OPM.
Key downside risks: 1) supply chain risks; 2) weaker semi client demand; and 3)

weaker-than-expected product expansion.
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of NT$833 is based on a 15.4x 2030E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 12.6%. Our target multiple is derived from peers’
correlation between forward-year trading P/E and earnings growth.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition, technology migration
trends in optical networking, and slower-than-expected capacity ramp-up.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - VPEC

Valuation: We adopt a discounted P/E method and apply a 22.2x target P/E on VPEC’s
2029E EPS, discounting back to 2027E at a COE of 10.5% (beta 1.7x, risk free rate 1.6%
and market risk premium at 5.1%), to derive our 12m TP of NT$793. Our target P/E is
based on a 0.4x PEG&M ratio derived from the average level of peers in the photonics
supply chain.
Key risk: Slower-than-expected SiPh business ramp up; weaker-than-expected
microelectronics demand from smartphones clients; IDM offers EPI wafer in-house.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - RoboTechnik
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of Rmb796 is based on a 20.7x 2031E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 11.3%. Our target multiple is derived from the
correlation between consumer electronic peers’ PEG&M (2026E P/E to 2027E NI YoY and
OPM), with RoboTechnik’s 2032E net income at 2% YoY and 2032E OPM at 32%.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition; lower-than-expected

optical connection end demand; worse-than-expected photovoltaic market downcycle.

In this report, we focus on E Ink's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for its share price.

• August sales were NT$3,446mn (+20% MoM/+3% YoY).
• QTD sales reached 63% of our 3Q26 revenue estimate of NT$9,985mn (-2%
QoQ/-4% YoY) and 62% of consensus at NT$10,213mn (flat QoQ/-2% YoY).
Our view:
• The solid rebound in the Aug monthly sales should alleviate the potential

risk of missing full-year guidance again (now at 10-15% YoY for 2026), in our
view, as  3Q26 revenue is tracking in line with our estimate for  a modest
decline QoQ.
• While the worst seems to be behind us and valuation is at a trough level of
12x 2027 P/E, we see no strong catalysts in the near term, despite our
positive long-term view on  e-paper demand across various applications.

E Ink Holdings Inc. (8069.TWO)

ings growth momentum. We view our target multiple of 12x as fair, considering our estimated

### Page 1

Wistron

Reiterate Buy: Aug sales +49% MoM, aided 
by solid AI momentum; lift PO to NT$265

Reiterate Rating: BUY | PO: 265.00 TWD | Price: 189.00 TWD

Aug’26 sales +49% MoM, mainly driven by AI 
Wistron’s Aug’26 sales of NT$460bn grew 49% MoM (+166% YoY), with subsidiary 
Wiwynn’s Aug sales of NT$144bn grew 23% MoM (+50% YoY). Wistron’s strong Aug 
sales were mainly driven by enterprise AI server projects, with overall AI server rack 
shipments roughly doubling MoM. Given the strong Aug sales, we lift our 3Q26 sales 
forecast by 11%. We expect Sep sales to decline 20% MoM to NT$370bn from the high 
Aug base. Yet, Sep sales should remain above July’s NT$308bn as we stay positive on AI 
order momentum into following quarters, driven by Nvidia’s new Vera Rubin generation.  
PC remains soft; Aug shipments down 13% MoM 
Wistron’s Aug NB shipments were 1.4mn (-13% MoM, -36% YoY). We view it as in line 
with supply chain’s commentary on weaker demand in 2H26 amid continued component 
cost inflation issue. This also echoes Wistron management’s cautious tone that PC 
shipment should decline 10-20% HoH in 2H26 following earlier order pull-in 1H26. We 
now expect 3Q26 NB shipment to fall 18% QoQ, implying 1.5mn units of NB shipments 
in Sep (+8% MoM, -31% YoY) with potential quarter-end pull-in demand. 
Lift PO to NT$265; reiterate Buy on solid AI momentum 
We lift our 2026-28E EPS by 4-6% to reflect higher sales, mainly driven by AI (with 
diversifying clients/projects), better operating leverage, and actual 2Q26 data. We raise 
our PO to NT$265 from NT$238, with our valuation method unchanged at 15x 2H26-
1H27E EPS. We reiterate Buy on Wistron’s solid multi-year AI server outlook. We expect 
a positive near-term market reaction to the strong Aug sales.

Company Sector 
IT Hardware

Company Description 
Wistron is one of the top-5 ODMs globally. Server/storage 
and PC business accounted for 73% and 24% of sales in 
2025, respectively. Key server/storage customers include 
Dell, Lenovo, HPE, Cisco, Nvidia, AMD, Intel. Key NB 
customers include Dell, Lenovo, Acer. Wistron was spun off 
from Acer (2353 TT) in 2000 and was incorporated in May 
2001. It went publicly listed on the Taiwan stock exchange 
in Aug 2003. It is headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan.

Investment Rationale 
We assign a Buy rating to Wistron in view of improving 
sales/profit mix, solid outlook from Wiwynn, high exposure 
to server business after exiting from low-margin iPhone 
assembly business, and improving OPM. We believe 
Wistron will benefit from Dell's strong demand in Nvidia AI 
GPU server rack as the key supplier.

### Page 7

Price objective basis & risk 
Wistron (WICOF) 
Our PO of NT$265 is based on 15x 2H26-1H27E EPS. We use 15x valuation multiple 
(around 1.5SD above historical P/E average since 2022) in view of high server mix, a key 
position in AI server supply chain with exposure both to component/rack business, and 
ongoing OPM improvement.

Upside risks to our PO are (1) stronger server market demand, especially for AI, (2) 
stronger PC demand, (3) share/order win in AI server business, and (4) favorable FX 
trend.

Downside risks to our PO are (1) softer AI server demand due to AI GPU short supply or 
supply chain hiccup, (2) weaker PC market demand amid inflation/macro uncertainties, 
(3) GM pressure due to higher labor/logistics cost, (4) more intensified competition in 
NB and server business, and (5) unfavorable FX movement (USD/RMB and/or USD/NTD) 
to weigh on GM and/or non-operating items.

AI semi capex, in particular for compute chips, should outgrow
overall AI capex in 2028. We add cross-checks on ASICs after
AVGO’s guidance and the Qualcomm/AWS AI ASIC
announcement.
Will 2028 be another growth year for AI semis? Our US internet analyst Brian
Nowak published the Morgan Stanley AI Guidebook: Navigating the Age of
Inference, and suggests 12% CSP capex growth into 2028, raising investor questions
about AI semi growth momentum. Based on our latest supply chain checks, we

introduce preliminary 2028 CoWoS/CoPoS/EMIB-T capacity assumptions. In
aggregate, we still see 50% capacity growth in 2028 (see Exhibit 1), implying
flattish infrastructure (e.g., the shell and AI DC) spending and moderate memory
pricing in 2028.
Larger chip size and more applications (CPU, networking) to drive further
growth in 2028: All these packaging technologies are 2.5D (compute and memory
chips on side to side) for AI/HPC chips, including AI GPU, XPU, CPU, and networking.

•CoWoS (wafer based): We still see some CoW expansion at TSMC. For oS, TSMC
may need more partners than ASE. Our checks suggest both Amkor and Xintec
(non-covered) will diversify oS production in the US and Taiwan, respectively.
• CoPoS (panel-based): This is a panel-level process. After converting to 12-inch
CoWoS wafer equivalents, we assume 5–10kwpm in 2028. The initial target project
should be Nvidia’s Feynman Ultra GPU.
• EMIB-T (substrate-based): Although a substrate-based technology, we convert it

to 12-inch CoWoS wafer-equivalent capacity as well. One EMIB-T substrate can
generate 16 pcs of a 9x reticle-size chip, around 4x the chips a CoWoS wafer can
generate. Our checks indicate ~40k–45k wafer-equivalent EMIB-T capacity in 2028,
producing at least 2mn of Humufish (9x reticle) substrates. 40k–45k wafer
equivalents also imply 10-15% share in 2.5D packaging.
Read-across from recent ASIC guidance at Broadcom and the Qualcomm/AWS
partnership

•According to Joe Moore’s report: Broadcom Inc.: Earnings solid; raising FY 28 EPS,
more specific FY27 revenue guidance is now US$115 bn, and that could double again
in FY28. Our CoWoS supply-chain checks already see an AVGO AI lab customer
booking ~15k–30k CoWoS wafers for 2027.
•Qualcomm announced its ASIC partnership with AWS, a key Alchip ASIC customer.
However, the press release points to inference, different from Alchip’s Trainium4,
which covers both training and inference. We therefore see limited impact to Alchip.

TSMC CoWoS and CoPoS
With continual booming demand in AI, we expect TSMC and its OSAT partners to expedite
capacity expansion plans for CoWoS. We expect TSMC's CoWoS capacity to further build
to 260kwpm in 2028 from 130/200kwpm in 2026/2027, with 2028's expansion mainly

focusing in Arizona's AP9/10 and potentially in AP7. TSMC is now conducting trial
production for CoPoS in Taoyuan. As long as the progress goes well, we expect TSMC to
start building its CoPoS capacity, with the location also likely to be in AP9/10 or AP7P3.
We expect the non-TSMC camp to expand CoWoS capacity to 110kwpm by 2028 year-end
from 80kwpm by end-2027. For ASE/SPIL, we expect FoCoS+CoWoS capacity to rise from
30kwpm at 2027-end to 50-60kwpm at 2028-end, with expansion focused on CoWoS-L

and CoWoS-R. For Amkor, we expect CoWoS capacity to increase from 30kwpm at 2027-
end to 55-60kwpm at 2028-end, also focused on CoWoS-L and CoWoS-R.

while 38% below our estimates, and we attribute it to the muted growth of wearable 
hinges and Notebook hinges. However, we remain positive on company’s new projects, 
and expects to see MoM/ QoQ growth recovery ahead on clients’ new products launch 
and better seasonality to reflect on company’s growth.

### Page 3

Earnings revision: We factor in SZS Aug revenues, revise down 2026E earnings by 11%, 
revise up 2027E earnings by 1%, and keep 2028E earnings largely unchanged. We revise 
down 2026E revenues mainly on lower-than-expected Aug revenues, considering longer 
time for new projects to reflect on company’s revenues/ earnings. We revise up 2027 
earnings mainly on higher revenues, reflecting our positive view on SZS as the key 
beneficiary of rising foldable phones.

Valuation: We are Buy rated on SZS with a 12-month target price of NT$300 (vs. 
previously at NT$286) on lower earnings. Our TP is based on a 21.9x 2027E P/E (vs. 
previously at 21.0x), which is derived from the updated sector correlation of 2027E P/E 
vs. 2027E-28E EPS YoY (Exhibit 8), with re-rating supported by positive view on rising 
foldable phone penetration. The 21.9x 2027E P/E is also within SZS’s trading range since 
Aug 2019.

### Page 4

Price Target Risks and Methodology - SZS 
Valuation: We use a near-term P/E vs. EPS growth correlation to derive our target price 
for SZS, consistent with our Taiwan Technology coverage. Our target 2027E P/E multiple 
of 21.9x for SZS is based on the sector correlation of 2027E P/E vs. 2027-28E earnings 
growth. We thus derive our 12-month target price at NT$300. We are Buy rated. Key 
risks: Weaker-than-expected headset hinges demand; slower-than-expected foldable 
phone penetration; potential competition from more suppliers; soft market demand.

### Page 1

Taiwan Information Technology

What’s new: We provide our update on Aspeed following its upbeat 4Q26 
revenue guidance on 4 September. We believe the strong guidance 
reaffirms our positive view that agentic AI has served as a catalyst for end 
demand for regular servers starting early 2026. Baseboard management 
controller (BMC) shipments for general servers (AI and non-AI together) 
should grow c.50% YoY in 2026. We believe that the new 4Q26 revenue 
guidance implies regular server shipment volume will increase c.50% YoY 
in 2027, hence the 36/34% uplift in our 2027/28E earnings forecasts.

What’s the impact: Solid regular server shipments ahead. Aspeed’s 
latest guidance range for its 4Q26 sales at TWD6.6-6.8bn implies 4Q26 
BMC shipments of c.12m. With this run-rate, total BMC shipments in 2027 
should be near c.50m, much higher than our previous estimate of 36.1m. 
We attribute the ongoing strength to agentic AI and AI-related general-
purpose demand. We forecast Aspeed’s BMC for general servers to 
increase to 27m in 2027E (from 18m in 2026E and 13m in 2025). At the 
same time, we expect BMC for AI servers to increase c.50% to 20m in 
2027E (up from 13m in 2026E and 5m in 2025). To sum up, we now 
forecast BMC shipments of 32.7m in 2026 and 47.6m in 2027 (+46% YoY 
in 2027). Based on our AI-related general server assumptions (excluding 
non-AI general servers), we expect the CPU:XPU ratio to rise to 1:1.3 in 
2027E (from 1:2.6 in 2026E). We expect a rising CPU:XPU ratio to become 
a key growth driver and share-price catalyst in the years after 2027. Due to 
the solid end demand, management is considering adjusting its pricing 
again from November to factor in the additional packaging cost, leading to 
our higher gross margin assumptions from 4Q26.

New growth opportunities. Following our visits to Aspeed’s booth at 
Computex 2026 and the OCP APAC conference, we believe Aspeed will 
continually maximise the dollar content per server board. Compared with 
last year’s version (embedded software-defined FPGA), Aspeed is 
integrating a Lattice FPGA into its next-generation Bridge IC (SMC; 
AST1840), which should support higher ASPs for its products.

What we recommend: We lift our 2026-28E EPS by 9-36% to factor in our 
higher BMC shipment assumptions. We lift our 12M TP to TWD26,660 
(from TWD19,800), based on an unchanged PER of 66x (high end of its 
past-3-year PER range of 21-78x), applied to our 1-year forward EPS 
forecast. Our 2025-28E EPS CAGR of 83% makes our target PER 
undemanding, given the resulting PEG ratio of 0.8. Key downside risk: 
weak AI server demand.

How we differ: Our 2026-28E EPS are 6-26% higher than the consensus, 
likely due to our bullish view on Aspeed’s ASP and shipment story.

14 September 2026

Promising outlook on agentic AI

➢ Rising CPU:XPU ratio is becoming a key growth driver for Aspeed… 
➢ … which indicates solid regular server demand despite supply hiccups 
➢ Reaffirming our Buy (1) rating and raising 12-month TP to TWD26,660

Company profile 
Established in November 2004, Aspeed is a fabless IC design company specialising in baseboard 
management controllers (BMCs), which are mostly used for the remote management of servers. Aspeed 
is a global leader in BMC, with about 70% market share. Its other products include PC/AV extension 
SoC, which supports the extension of digital signals of PCs or multimedia content to remote terminals; 
and Cupola360, which is a spherical image processor that supports 360-degree cameras.

ESG analysis

Update Date: 14 Sep 2026 
Source: Daiwa, Company

ESG risks
Risks Management Analyst comments
G
Executive/board
quality 2
Aspeed’sboard consists of 9 directors, with 4 independent directors. The directors’backgrounds
appear to have a high correlation to semiconductors (either education or work experience),
which we see as a positive for executive quality. In 2025, Aspeed held 6 board meetings and the
average attendee rate was 100%. Given Aspeed’sChairman is also the CEO, we think it is a
negative factor for board/executive management as well as external shareholders.
Capital management 1
Aspeed declared a DPS of TWD80 in 2025, representing an 77% payout ratio. Being a leading
global board management controller (BMC) IC design vendor with c.70% market share globally,
the company’sleading position and asset-light model (major expenses are from R&D
employees) allow it to maintain high ROE/ROA ratios and a high dividend payout policy. BMC IC
recently penetrated new applications (such as power supply, storage, edge servers), which can
improve its profitability on a higher revenue scale, in our view.
Related party &
transaction 2
In 2025, there were no sales to or purchases from related parties. In previous years, the main
purchases from related parties was from Avago. After selling its fully-owned Emulex unit to
Aspeed, Avago (Broadcom) became an Aspeed's shareholder with a c.6% stake in 2016. We
believe the bargaining power from its 6% shareholding was not sufficient to preload its IC
products on Aspeed's products or earn unfair profits. In any case, this relationship ended in
February 2021. As such, we see limited risk from related-party transactions.
S Supply chain
management 1
Aspeed ensures that suppliers comply with social responsibility, green environmental protection,
occupational safety and health, human rights and RBA, and prefer to work with ISO9001,
ISO14001 and ISO45001 certified suppliers. In addition, every Aspeed supplier is required to
issue a publicly disclosed sustainability management report.
E Water & wastewater
management 1
Being a fabless IC design company, Aspeed’sbusiness doesn’tinvolve a production process.
According to the company's data, it produced 4,035 tonnes of wastewater in 2025. As such, we
see limited risk from its water and waste water management.
E
Waste & hazardous
materials
management
1
Being a fabless IC design company, Aspeed’sbusiness doesn’tinvolve production processes
that may produce hazardous materials. That said, the company indicated it would employ green
design concepts and simplified product structures throughout its R&D process in order to reduce
pollution. As such, we see limited risk from its waste and hazardous materials management.
E GHG emissions 1
Due to its fabless business model, Aspeed produces limited emissions of GHG, wastewater, and
waste materials each year. According to the company’sdata, it produced around 273.5 tonnes of
CO2 in 2025.
Note: Management score represents a company's ability to manage/benefit from certain ESG topics. The scores range from 1 to 3, with 1 being the strongest.

Industry View In-Line
Overall August ODM notebook shipments came in 19% below our estimate: Pull-
forward demand appears to have come to an end, channel partners and distributors
have stocked up on inventory, and OEMs are slowing their sales into the channel.
We believe this is the main reason why August NB builds came in slower than our

expectation. However, we continue to expect product mix to continue to shift
toward higher-end, more-profitable models. Several ODMs such as Quanta and
Compal have even lowered 3Q NB build forecasts compared to their earlier guidance
on 2Q earnings calls three weeks ago. Thus we lower our 3Q NB build estimate by
7% to 25.4M units (-16% q/q, -25% y/y). This sequential decline is sub-seasonal vs.
the 15-year average seasonality of +5% q/q in 3Q, and implies September NB builds

at 9.9M units (+35% m/m, -18% y/y).
We introduce our 4Q notebook build estimate at 23.9M units (-6% q/q, -26% y/
y): This sequential decline is sub-seasonal (despite an already lowered base in 3Q)
vs. the 15-year average seasonality of flat q/q in 4Q. None of the ODMs have
provided official guidance for 4Q notebook builds, but our preliminary checks
suggests that they will continue to fall q/q. On our estimate, this implies that the
top 5 Taiwan NB ODMs' builds for CY26 will come in at ~108.8M units (-16% y/

communications with a subject company, public appearances

Key Takeaways
Top five ODMs' August 2026 NB shipments were 7.3M units (-11% m/m, -35% y/y),
19% below our estimate.
We see September 2026 NB builds at 9.9M units (+35% m/m, -18% y/y).
We lower our 3Q26 NB build estimate by 7% to 25.4M units (-16% q/q, -25% y/y).
We introduce our 4Q26 NB build estimate at 23.9M units (-6% q/q, -26% y/y).

Our top five ODMs' CY26 NB build estimate is ~108.8M units (-16% y/y).

### Page 2

M
Japan Insight
2
Investment Perspective
MLCC is early cycle in AI server & rack penetration
There is immense change underway for the MLCC industry with an investment narrative
that is changing as AI chips/server demand is increasingly driving MLCC scarcity.  AI is
shifting from semiconductors to MLCCs, creating a supply/demand mismatch in high-end
components. The high-end AI MLCC market is effectively a Japanese-Korean duopoly with
Murata and SEMCO together hold around 85% share. High-capacitance, low-ESL parts for

AI accelerators require hundreds to over a thousand dielectric layers with near-zero
defects and face strict customer qualification — the barrier preventing a repeat of 2017-
18, when shortages invited entry and the cycle self-corrected. AI platforms now compete
directly with consumer, automotive, and industrial applications for advanced materials,
heightening supply risk for MLCC traditional customers. We are still in the early innings,
and supply concerns are extending beyond near-term shortages to longer-term supply

security. As a result, we are seeing an increasing number of long-term supply agreements
being signed between suppliers and customers.
Exhibit 1: Sequencing the technology cycle – still early cycle for MLCC
Source:  Morgan Stanley Research estimates
Turning point in MLCC pricing
While Murata Mfg.’s CFO and Executive Deputy President Masanori Minamide stated in a
Sep 14 Nikkei interview that rising production loads for high-end products are making it

increasingly difficult to fully supply low-end products, and that the priority of defending
low-end market share has effectively declined, we believe the company’s fundamental
policy of not changing prices based solely on short-term supply-demand conditions
remains intact. That said, in our view, Murata has been gradually shifting its strategy
toward focusing more on its areas of strength and adopting pricing that better reflects the
need to cover large-scale capital investments, particularly in those core segments where it

enjoys a competitive advantage. We believe that Murata’s reluctance to enter into L TAs for
AI/data-center use value added MLCCs reflects its view that locking in prices today may
not be optimal, given the potential for MLCC pricing to rise in the future.
We expect sales growth to continue for small-sized, high-
capacity, high-value-added MLCCs for AI servers/DCs

### Page 3

M
Japan Insight
Morgan Stanley MUFG 3
MLCCs are a key business, accounting for 50% of sales at Murata, 46% at SEMCO, 19% at
Yageo, and 70% at Taiyo Yuden in 2025. We expect global MLCC shipment value to
expand at a CAGR of 20.3%, from $18.51bn in 2025 to $44.45bn in 2031. We believe
growth is set to accelerate from the 5.0% CAGR recorded in global MLCC shipment value
over the 13 years of 2012-25 because we expect continued growth in sales of small, high-

capacity, high-value-added MLCCs for AI servers/datacenters (DCs) from 2026. For AI
servers/DCs alone, we forecast MLCC shipment value to reach $23.33bn by 2031 (vs. our
previous estimate of $10.80bn), implying a 57.1% CAGR (vs. 38.1%).
Howard Kao (our Greater China Technology Hardware analyst) expects MLCC demand
volume for VR200 NVL72 racks to increase about 80% versus GB300 NVL72 racks, and
forecasts the number of MLCCs mounted in each Rubin NVL72 rack will jump to roughly

570,000 units from around 320,000 for GB300 NVL72 racks, with MLCC dollar content
per rack estimated to increase by 166%.　We expect the rapid expansion of the high-value-
added MLCC market for AI servers/DCs to be especially positive for  earnings at Murata (#1
market share in MLCCs for 2025 at 41%) and SEMCO (#2 at 23%).

Key roles of MLCCs in AI/DC
MLCCs play a role in locally stabilizing power supply (instantaneous current supply plus

noise removal) near semiconductors, such as GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. Since GPUs, CPUs,
and FPGAs repeatedly switch on and off on a nanosecond timescale, they demand large
currents instantaneously, and MLCCs meet this instantaneous current demand by
immediately discharging their stored charge. As semiconductor miniaturization advances,
circuit operating speed increases and drive voltage falls. As voltage decreases, even small
voltage fluctuations risk causing semiconductor malfunction, so even more stable power

supply voltage is required than before. Demand for capacitor capacitance is also increasing
in line with AI servers' rising computing power and power consumption, and because
board area and mountable space are limited, we expect demand for smaller, higher-
capacity MLCCs to persist.
Sharp dips vs. share price peaks provide re-entry opportunity
Year-to-date to Sep 11, share prices of the four companies had risen 127% for Murata,
449% for SEMCO, 141% for Yageo, and 160% for Taiyo Yuden. However, from their

respective June-July peaks, these have fallen 40% for Murata, 38% for SEMCO, 52% for

### Page 4

M
Japan Insight
4
Yageo, and 59% for Taiyo Yuden. Considering the strong likelihood that high-value-added
products for AI servers/DCs will continue to drive growth in MLCC demand not only in
2026 but also from 2027 onward, and that each company's earnings will stay on an
expansionary trend, we believe the conditions are now in place to consider re-entering
these stocks.

AI/DC MLCC market to continue growing at a rapid pace
We expect growth in demand to accelerate for high-value-added products for AI/DC from

the second half of 2026. Howard Kao  expects MLCC demand volume for VR200 NVL72
racks to increase about 80% versus GB300 NVL72 racks, and forecasts the number of
MLCCs mounted in each Rubin NVL72 rack will rise sharply to roughly 570,000 units from
around 320,000 units for GB300 NVL72 racks (Exhibit 11 ). This increase stems from a
rise in the number of MLCCs mounted on both compute boards and switch boards, as well
as an increase in PCB content across the overall system, including modules such as CX9

Orchid. Howard Kao estimates this increase in MLCC mounting volume will lift the dollar-
based MLCC content per rack by 166% ( Exhibit 12 ).

Role of MLCCs in AI servers
Capacitors, including multi-layer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), function as a “dam” that
temporarily stores electricity, and are an essential electronic component for noise removal

and voltage stabilization in virtually all electronic circuits, including those used in
computers, smartphones, and automobiles. MLCCs play a role in locally stabilizing power
supply (instantaneous current supply plus noise removal) near semiconductors such as
GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. Since GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs repeatedly switch on and off on a
nanosecond timescale, they demand large currents instantaneously, and MLCCs meet this
instantaneous current demand by immediately discharging their stored charge. At the

same time, MLCCs bypass only the AC component (noise and fluctuating current), which
also serves to prevent noise from entering GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. MLCCs feature low
ESR (low resistance) and low ESL (low inductance), allowing them to track even

### Page 10

M
Japan Insight
10
nanosecond-level current fluctuations in semiconductors such as GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. 
MLCCs are often placed around components such as GPUs and ASICs that operate at low 
voltages of around 1.0V. As semiconductor miniaturization advances, circuit operating 
speed increases and drive voltage falls. As voltage decreases, even small voltage 
fluctuations risk causing semiconductor malfunction, requiring an even more stable power 
supply voltage than before. Demand for capacitor capacitance will also rise along with AI 
servers' improving computing power and increasing power consumption, and because 
board area and mountable space are limited, demand for smaller, higher-capacity MLCCs 
will likely continue. 
MLCC miniaturization and higher capacity to accelerate with 
VR200 NVL72
We assume that the space available for mounting MLCCs on VR200 NVL72 will not 
change significantly from the GB300 NVL72 rack, and that the transition from GB300 to 
VR200 will require installing higher-capacity MLCCs within the limited space of 
semiconductor ABF package substrates and AI accelerator boards, accelerating growth in 
demand for small-sized, high-capacity MLCCs. Murata has consistently been a leader in 
MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases, beginning mass production of 1005-size 1 F 
MLCCs in 2000 and 0402-size 1 F and 1005-size 22 F MLCCs in 2020. We expect 
demand for 1608-size 100 F, 1005-size 47 F, and 0603-size 10 F MLCCs to increase 
substantially with VR200 NVL72. We estimate that 1608-size 100 F MLCCs command a 
unit price 5-10x higher than 2012-size 100 F or 1608-size 47 F MLCCs, and we expect 
the shift to smaller, higher-capacity MLCCs accompanying the transition to VR200 NVL72 
to drive a substantial rise in ASP.

incremental opportunity: Our analysis suggests that 47µF+ MLCCs could account for

capacitance devices within AI accelerator systems and a growing mix shift toward higher-

From a volume perspective, we estimate Cloud AI demand for 47µF+ MLCCs could 
increase from approximately 4 billion units in CY25 to 40B+ units by CY27: Such a 
rapid increase would represent a meaningful step-up in industry demand and could require 
substantial capacity reallocation or expansion among leading suppliers.
Based on our industry discussions, the market for high-capacitance MLCCs remains 
concentrated among a limited number of suppliers, primarily Japanese and Korean 
manufacturers, including Murata, Taiyo Yuden, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO). 
As demand from AI infrastructure accelerates, we believe capacity utilization for these 
products could tighten, raising the possibility of capacity crowding-out effects across 
other end markets and applications.

Materials development and production technology behind
MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases
In MLCCs, smaller sizes and higher capacities have mainly been achieved by thinning the
dielectric and electrode layers (layer thinning) and increasing the number of layers
stacked (multilayering). For high-capacity products for AI/DC, in addition to the layer
thinning and multilayering described above, efforts are accelerating to further miniaturize

and increase capacity by expanding the area of the dielectric and internal electrodes per
dielectric sheet. We believe MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases depend on: (1)
developing superior dielectric and electrode materials; (2) manufacturing highly uniform,
highly reliable slurry; (3) technology for precisely　stacking dielectric sheets; and (4)
technology for firing in a controlled atmosphere without oxidation. For high-capacity
products for AI/DC, we see the key factors as (1) materials development that increases the

crystallinity of dielectric materials while making them finer, in order to thin each dielectric
layer as much as possible (layer thinning), together with (2) manufacturing technology to
precisely stack the dielectric sheets.

Dielectric material manufacturing process
Dielectric materials are manufactured by adding a binder, solvent, and additives to barium
titanate (BaTiO3), which is produced from barium carbonate (B aCO3) and titanium oxide

(TiO2). Methods for manufacturing barium titanate are broadly divided into the solid-
phase method and the liquid-phase method. In the solid-phase method, barium carbonate
and titanium oxide are mixed and fired at high temperature, producing barium titanate
through a chemical reaction at the firing stage. In the liquid-phase method, barium
carbonate and titanium oxide are dissolved in a solution, reacted at the solution stage, and
fired at a relatively low temperature to produce the compound. Manufacturing methods

used in mass production via the liquid-phase method include the oxalate method and the
hydrothermal synthesis method. Barium titanate with small and uniform particle size is
key to smaller and higher-capacity MLCCs. In 2023, Murata established MF Materials, a
joint venture with Ishihara Sangyo and Ishihara Sangyo's wholly owned subsidiary Fuji
Titanium (with equity stakes of 20% for Murata, 10% for Ishihara Sangyo, and 70% for Fuji
Titanium). MF Materials produces barium titanate via the oxalate process and supplies it

to Murata Manufacturing.　MF Materials is constructing a new building adjacent to its head
office plant in Nobeoka, Miyazaki Prefecture, with operations scheduled to commence in
2027. TDK established a joint venture with Nippon Chemical Industrial in April 2026 called
TDK-NCI Advanced Materials (with equity stakes of 51% for TDK and 49% for Nippon
Chemical Industrial), with plans to accelerate development of the oxalate method barium
titanate.

Murata and SEMCO to benefit the most from growing
demand for high-value-added products for AI servers
We expect Murata and SEMCO, which supply small, high-capacity products stably and in
large volumes, to capture the greatest benefits from growing demand for small-sized,
high-capacity MLCCs used in AI servers and data centers. Murata has explained that AI/DC

MLCC sales accounted for 10-15% of its MLCC sales in F3/26 and are forecast to rise 100-
105% YoY in F3/27, accounting for 20-25% of MLCC sales. We estimate Murata's AI/DC
MLCC sales to rise roughly 120% YoY in F3/27 and about 100% YoY in F3/28, with AI/DC
MLCCs underpinning growth in the company's overall MLCC sales. Murata has stated that
it forecasts a 100-105% increase in AI/DC MLCC sales in F3/27, reflecting a roughly 40%
increase in volume and a roughly 50% rise in ASP, but we expect the increase in ASP to

exceed its forecast.

What are the risks to Murata?
Risks for Murata include: (1) losing MLCC market share by failing to adequately supply
MLCCs for AI servers/DCs amid rapidly expanding demand. (2) Murata's products,
including MLCCs, are used not only in AI servers/DCs but across virtually all electronic
equipment, including automobiles, smartphones, and industrial machinery, making the
company sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and inventory cycles. (3) The company

has explained that a ¥1/$ appreciation of the yen would reduce operating profit by ¥4.5bn

Murata’s share price risk/reward: Even though we raise our earnings estimates for

Murata, we lower our DCF-based price target from ¥12,500 to ¥11,000, mainly reflecting
an increase in our DCF model’s risk-free rate from 2.60% to 3.0%. Murata's share price has
fallen 41% year-to-date from its June 22 peak, and we see 53% upside over the next 12-18
months, maintain our OW rating, and designate the stock as our Top Pick in Japan's
electronic components industry. The reasons are as follows: (1) We forecast the dollar-
based shipment value of MLCCs, where Murata held the top global share of 40% in 2025,

to expand at a CAGR of 21% through 2031, with Murata continuing to gradually gain
market share. (2) Demand for MLCCs used in AI servers/DCs is likely to continue
expanding, and demand for small, high-capacity, high-value-added products, which Murata
has brought to market ahead of competitors, should grow substantially. (3) Outside of
MLCCs, we look for demand to expand for small, high-value-added products, including
secondary batteries for DC BBUs, power modules for vertical power delivery in AI servers,

and RF modules for smartphones, and then expand even further as edge AI devices

become widespread. (4) In addition to earnings growth, we expect that management’s
proactive approach to shareholder returns, including share buybacks, will raise capital
efficiency and lift ROE.
Bull case ¥14,000, 95% projected upside
In our bull case, we assume higher sales of MLCCs for AI servers/data centers than in our
base case, for component sales of 7% higher than our base case, for OP of ¥560.3bn in
F3/27, ¥794bn in F3/28, and ¥1.515tn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF

assumptions are the same as for our base case. Bull case fair value corresponds to 58.2x of
fully-diluted F3/27 EPS of ¥240.4, 41.1x fully-diluted F3/28 EPS of ¥340.7, and 21.1x fully-
diluted F3/31 EPS of ¥664.0.
Bear case ¥3,500
Murata products are used in all kinds of different electronic devices, and they are easily
affected by the macro economy and inventory cycle. In our bear case, we assume slower
global economic growth rates and lower production of high-end consumer goods like

high-end smartphones than in our base case for OP of ¥314.6bn in F3/27, ¥330bn in F3/28,
and ¥362.4bn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF assumptions are the same as in
our base case. Here we look for ROE to increase from 8.8% in F3/26 to 9.3% in F3/27 and
9.4% in F3/28, above capital cost of 7.5%. With profit below the market consensus, we
assume the share price falls to a P/B of 2.4x.

SEMCO earnings forecasts
Shawn Kim
AI-driven MLCC growth and pricing to drive sharp earnings
acceleration in FY27, with continued growth in FY28
FY26-28 forecasts: We project SEMCO OP of W2.34tn in FY26 (+156% YoY), W5.70tn in
FY27 and W8.36tn in FY28, implying further growth of 144% and 47%, respectively. We
expect the earnings acceleration to be driven mainly by the Components (MLCC) and
Package Solution businesses, while the Optics business remains a relatively modest

contributor. In FY27, our projected OP of W5.70tn breaks down as Components W4.56tn,
Package Solution W943bn, and Optics W201bn, versus W1.67tn, W510bn, and W165bn,
respectively, in FY26. In FY28, we forecast Components OP rising further to W6.55tn,
Package Solution to W1.58tn, and Optics to W230bn. As such, we expect SEMCO's consol.
OP margin to grow from 8.1% in FY25 to 15.7% in FY26, 24.5% in FY27, and 25.9% in FY28.
We maintain the stock as our top pick within our S. Korea Technology coverage.

For Components, we expect profit growth to accelerate as AI-server demand drives both
strong MLCC volume growth and a structurally richer product mix. High-end AI MLCC
supply remains tight, with lead times exceeding 20 weeks, supply-chain inventories lean
following two years of destocking, and book-to-bill at the three high-end suppliers
reaching its highest level since the pandemic. Importantly, contract pricing has increasingly
been institutionalized through long-term agreements, while the high-end AI MLCC market

remains concentrated, with Murata and SEMCO together holding around 85% share.
Capacity additions are also unlikely to close the supply-demand gap quickly, as most
meaningful new capacity is scheduled for 2027 or later and suppliers are generally
targeting only around 10-15% annual output growth. We thus expect tighter supply-
demand, higher pricing, and a shift toward high-capacitance, low-ESL AI products to drive
Components OP margin from 21.4% in FY26 to 30.9% in FY27 and 30.1% in FY28.

Bull case W3,000,000
Our bull case assumes ABF opportunities from major US CSPs drive stronger content
growth, with future ASIC content & volume growth continuing to outpace our base-case
expectations. Customer diversification toward non-mobile customers should also reduce
earnings volatility and improve profitability. Our bull case, equivalent to 15x FY27e P/B,
reflects what we see as an unprecedented super-cycle in the underlying AI-related MLCC

and ABF markets.
Bear case W1,350,000
In our bear case, we assume slower content growth in MLCCs and substrates due to
greater competition and China's localization, together with prolonged consumer weakness
weighing on the Optics business. However, we still expect increasing AI exposure to
structurally lift SEMCO's MLCC and ABF ASPs, product mix and margins, given the
difficulty commodity suppliers face in penetrating the premium market. Our bear-case

value corresponds to 7x FY27e P/B. Key downside risks include a significant pullback in

Chinese smartphone customers, and continued consumer-demand weakness.

stronger AI-related demand, with a more modest contribution from consumer
applications. This demand strength should support broad-based utilization improvement
across Yageo’s passive component portfolio. Pricing is also turning more favorable, with
distributor price increases implemented in 2Q26 and Yageo raising prices for direct

customers in 3Q26, as previously highlighted. The combination of higher utilization and
firmer pricing should drive meaningful operating leverage. We forecast gross margin
expanding to 39.3%, up 310bps y/y, and operating margin reaching 27.4%, up 500bps y/y,
supporting EPS of approximately NT$19.79.
Looking into CY27, we expect supply/demand conditions in the mid- and low-end markets
to tighten further, sustaining pricing momentum and driving an additional improvement in

utilization. We therefore forecast revenue of approximately NT$252B, up 38% y/y.
Continued operating leverage should lift gross margin to 43.2%, an increase of 390bps y/y,
and operating margin to 33.4%, up 600bps y/y, resulting in EPS of approximately NT$32.11.
Why has the stock been so volatile?
Yageo benefited from a sharp increase in MLCC pricing in 2Q26, driven by a temporary
spike in spot-market demand. In our view, ODM/EMS customers accelerated inventory

replenishment amid concerns that the ramp in high-end AI-server MLCC demand,
particularly alongside Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform, could constrain supply of mid- and
low-end MLCCs. Under normal market conditions, these customers typically carry only 3-4
weeks of inventory. However, supply concerns prompted a rapid increase in inventory
coverage to approximately 4-6 months.
During this restocking phase, ODM/EMS customers sourced MLCCs from both
manufacturers, including Yageo, and distributors. The resulting demand surge drove a

sharp increase in spot/distributor pricing and also contributed to the stock’s strong
performance. However, the pricing move was largely driven by a one-off inventory build.
Once customers had secured sufficient inventory, purchasing activity normalized and spot
pricing began to soften. This, together with weaker broader market sentiment, led to a
pullback of ~50% from the stock’s peak of approximately NT$1,140.
At the current share price, however, we believe the risk-reward has become attractive. The

underlying fundamentals, and, importantly, our view of the MLCC upcycle, remain intact.
Our analysis indicates substantial incremental demand for high-end, high-capacitance
MLCCs of 47µF and above, which will require a meaningful increase in dedicated
production capacity. We expect this to drive further capacity conversion toward high-end
MLCCs, with the resulting crowding-out effect becoming more visible from late CY26 into
early CY27. This should progressively tighten supply in the mid- and low-end MLCC

market and provide renewed support for pricing.

Price Target Discussion and Valuation Methodology
We lower our 12-month price target to NT$1,050 (from NT$1,465): This reflects our
lower earnings estimates for CY26-28. Our price target is our base case value, derived
from our residual income valuation model. Similar to our analysis of other tech hardware
companies within our coverage, we think this methodology provides the most accurate

value of the firm by taking into account the cost of equity.
Our key assumptions are:
• Cost of equity of 7.8%:
° Risk-free rate of 1.0% (10-year Taiwanese government bond yield);
° Equity risk premium of 6.8%;
° Beta of 1.1;

into active components. In addition, compared to global passive component peers, we

Our bull and bear case scenario values decrease by magnitudes similar to the change

We expect expect record profit in F3/29, not F3/28; upgrade
the stock from UW to EW
Full-term F3/27 and F3/28 earnings forecasts, F3/27 2Q forecasts: We project F3/27 OP
of ¥45.1bn (guidance ¥45bn, FactSet consensus ¥42bn), up +¥25.1bn YoY. We expect sales
in dollars of core product capacitors (MLCCs) to increase +22.6% YoY (+27.4% on yen
basis), a continued increase following on FY3/26’s +10.4% rise (+8.5% on yen basis), and

higher utilization rates absorbing increased depreciation expense and other fixed cost
increases. We project F3/28 OP of ¥66.1bn (consensus ¥73.1bn), up +¥25bn YoY. We look
for sales in dollars of capacitors (MLCCs) to rise +17.3% YoY (+16.6% on a yen basis),
absorbing increased depreciation expense and other fixed cost increases. We expect OP to
rise ¥83.8bn in F3/29 (consensus ¥107.1bn), surpassing the historical high profit of
¥68.2bn in F3/22.

We project 2Q OP of ¥12.6bn (consensus ¥11bn), up +¥7.8bn from ¥4.8bn in 1Q. We look
for MLCC sales to rise +18.1% compared with 1Q and for the utilization rate to rise from
85% in 1Q to 95% in 2Q. With increased sales of inductors for North American
smartphones, there should be a major profit increase on 1Q.

Taiyo Yuden share price risk/reward: We upgrade Taiyo Yuden from UW to EW, as we
believe its share price, having fallen 56.0% from its July 1 peak, has limited downside risk

and offers 6% upside over the next 12-18 months. We lower our DCF-based price target
from ¥12,500 to ¥10,500. This mainly reflects an increase in the DCF model’s risk-free
rate from 2.60% to 3.0%. We rate the stock EW rather than OW because: (1) In its core
MLCC business, we estimate Taiyo Yuden's MLCC market share was 11.3% in 2025, down
from 12.7% in 2020, and we think this downtrend continued into 2026, with its market
share shrinking to 10.7% in 1Q and 9.9% in 2Q. (2) We believe Taiyo Yuden is lagging

behind Murata (No. 1 share) and SEMCO (No. 2) in small, high-capacity MLCCs for AI
server accelerator boards, where demand is rapidly expanding. (3) We expect consensus
estimates for F3/28 onward to be revised down after 2Q results.
Bull case ¥14,000, 49% projected upside
In our bull case, F3/27 sales of MLCCs for AI servers/data centers are 7% higher than in our
base case, for OP of ¥56.5bn in F3/27, ¥85.5bn in F3/28, and ¥176.3bn in F3/31. Our forex

assumptions and DCF assumptions match our base case. Bull case fair value corresponds
to 50.7x our fully-diluted F3/27 EPS estimate of ¥276.1, 33.6x our fully-diluted F3/28 EPS
estimate of ¥417.0, and 15.9x our full-diluted F3/31 EPS estimate of ¥879.1.
Bear case ¥4,500
Taiyo Yuden’s care products (MLCCs and inductors) are used in all kinds of electronic
devices, and are easily affected by the macro economy and inventory cycle. In our bear
case, we assume slower global economic growth rates and lower production of high-end

consumer goods like high-end smartphones than in our base case, for OP of ¥39.2bn in
F3/27, ¥56.1bn in F3/28, and ¥65.8bn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF
assumptions are the same as in our base case. Here we look for ROE of 7.3% in F3/27 and
10.1% in F3/28, improving to a level above capital cost of 7.9%. With profit below market
expectations, we assume the share price falls to a P/B of 1.8x.

First Read
Voltronic Power
UBS Taiwan Summit 2026 key takeaways:
Earnings growth hinges on UPS/HVDC deliveries
Sales turning to growth in H226; sales mix change driving margin expansion
Management indicated bookings and shipments remained solid in July-Aug despite
temporary PCB shortages, and it expects a sales turnaround to growth in H226. Inverter
sales could stay weak on competition and Voltronic's product portfolio adjustments

(reducing low-margin products). Meanwhile, increasing outsourcing by brands will
support UPS sales growth. Management expects HVDC products to start contributing in
2027. Voltronic added a third customer for HVDC products. We think a higher sales
portion from UPS/HVDC products and inverter product adjustments could bring GM
expansion in 2027.
UPS growth intact;  HVDC and PDU represent the next legs of growth
The company expects sales to resume growth by single digits  in H226  and expects >10%

YoY growth in 2027. Management remains cautious about solar  inverters due to intense
competition from Chinese peers and expects inverter sales to decline as Voltronic adjusts
its product portfolio, focusing more on commercial solar  and premium products. For
2027, management expects offline UPS to grow 0-5%, supported by outsourcing
opportunities and emerging market demand, which could offset notebook weakness.
High-power UPS could account for an increasingly higher sales portion, driven by

accelerating outsourcing by tier 1 customers. For HVDC, management highlighted it
obtained one more client. HVDC product progress is on schedule, with 800VDC power
shelf sampling expected by year-end, a pilot run in H127 and mass production in H227.
The company is preparing testing and production equipment at factories in Taiwan and
China. Over the longer term, management also sees opportunities in PDUs, a market it
estimates at US$5bn in 2025, with a 12-15% sales CAGR over the next 5-8 years.

Margin  improvement on product mix optimisation and higher prices
Voltronic has implemented two UPS price increases this year to offset higher raw
material costs, which it expects to be reflected on its P&L starting in Sept 2026. For solar
inverters, management plans to focus on higher power and premium products with a
GM above 20%, while reducing low-power products with a GM at or below 20% over
the next two to three quarters, which could support GM expansion. In upcoming

quarters, solar inverter products may shrink to <20% of the total sales mix, while higher-
margin businesses such as high-power UPS and HVDC products continue to ramp. We
think the sales mix change will expand margins in 2027.
Valuation: Maintain Buy rating and PT of NT$1,128
We maintain our Buy rating and price target of NT$1,128, based on sum-of-the-parts
analysis, applying 28x/23x/24x 2027E PE for UPS/inverter/PSU business, respectively.

Company Description
Founded in 2008, Voltronic is a leading ODM for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) and
inverters. Its major customers include Schneider, Vertiv, and Riello. Voltronic is headquartered
in Taiwan and has production plants in mainland China, Vietnam, and Taiwan.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement

We base our price target on sum of the parts.
We believe the key risks for Voltronic include: 1) a slower-than-expected outsourcing trend
from leading branded UPS companies; 2) a faster-than-expected ramp-up of the electricity
grid in developing countries resulting in lower-than-expected demand for off-grid solar
systems; 3) FX risks; and 4) rising raw material prices.
Key industry-specific risks include: 1) unexpected changes in the underlying global

macroeconomic environment; 2) currency and interest rate movement; and 3) commodity
price inflation.

from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

收 發 模 組 出 貨 量 倍 增(2026~2028 年間 1.6T 光通訊 Trx 40~50% 
CAGR)。給 予 欣 興 投 資 建 議 維 持買 進 ， 目 標 價調整至 1,250 元(34.50x 
2027  EPS) 。

二.26 年營運概況 及 26 年展望  
1. 欣 興 受 惠ABF 產 業 供 需 吃 緊 ， 未 來 將 提 升 產 品 技 術 與 規 格 
根 據 載 板 廠 商 與 半 導 體 業 界 指 出 ， 日 後 將 追 隨 半 導 體 廠 發 展 異 質
整 合 封 裝、AiP (Antenna in Package) 、Info -on-Substrate(InFO -oS) 設計
或 先 進 封 裝 的 型 式 發 展 ， 欣 興 發 展 半 導 體 級 異 質 整 合 封 裝 ， 未 來
對 於 欣 興ABF 載 板 的 層 數 、 面 積 向 上 提 升 至 另 一 個 技 術 層 次 。此
外，Apple 自 製 其MacBook CPU 所 採 用 之 載 板 與 封 裝 集 成 設 計，Intel
之 外，AMD 也 同 步 發 表 其Chiplet 概 念，用 於 Server CPU 平 台 中 ，
包含 AMD EPYC Zen II 與 Gen 3rd Ryzen CPU ，新型 CPU 用 到 台 積
電 7nm 製程 性 能 提 升15% 以上 ，主 要 用 於 整 合Dram 與 其 他 I/O 介
面， 將 Chiplet 更 微 縮，Chiplet 小 晶 片 技 術 將 一 個 晶 片 組 成 的 處 理
器 劃 分 為 多 個 晶 片 ， 例 如 分 別 是 ： 數 據 存 儲 、 計 算 、 信 號 處 理 、
數 據 流 管 理 等 功 能，然 後 再 將 它 們 連 接 在 一 起 形 成 一 個「 小 晶 片 」
的 晶 片 網 絡 。 也 就 是 說 ， 未 來 的 電 腦 系 統 結 構 ， 可 能 只 包 含 一 個
CPU 晶 片 和 幾 個GPU，而 這 些 GPU 都 連 接 到 這 些Chiplet 晶 片 上 ，
形 成 晶 片 網 絡 。 換 言 之 ， 未 來 計 算 機 的 系 統 結 構 ， 可 能 不 是 由 單
獨 封 裝 的 晶 片 製 造 的，而 是 由IC 製 造 在 一 塊 較 大 的 矽 片 上 並 產 生
互 連 而 成 晶 片 網 絡。觀察 Intel(INTC) 、AMD(AMD) 其 整 合 型 封 裝觀
念 與 高 通(QCOM) 的將 Modem 晶 片 、AP 、 電 源 管 理IC(PWM IC) 、
天 線 及 超 音 波 感 測 等 技 術 區 塊，透 過 系 統 級SiP 封 裝 方 式 作 整 合 。
SiP 難 度 在 於 體 積 微 縮 以 外，還 要 整 合 不 同 的 封 裝 技 術，具 有 體 積
小 、 能 耗 低 、 開 發 週 期 短 、 質 量 輕 等 特 點， 具 有 異 曲 同 工 之 處 。
綜 合 上 述，台 積 電(2330) 替 Intel 代工 對 於 欣 興載 板 需 求更為 有 利 ，
短 期 內 欣 興 要 先 以 其三 鶯 廠 的 小 量ABF 供 應 給 Apple CPU 。

一. 預估 3Q26 稅後 EPS 1.33 元

為 38.72% 與 105.43% ，在產能滿載帶動，預估日成 KY 3Q26 營
收金額 9.00 億元， YoY+44.22% ，QoQ+39.31% ，預估營業利益
0.96 億元， YoY+185.3% ，QoQ+198.63% ，預估稅後盈餘 0.65
億元， YoY+199.85% ，QoQ+198.93% ，預估稅後 EPS 1.33 元。

二. 預估 4Q26 稅後 EPS 0.87 元 
進入 4Q26 傳統淡季，預估日成 KY 4Q26 營收金額 7.89 億元，
YoY+51.27% ， QoQ-12.33% ，預估營業利益 0.66 億元，
YoY+169.35% ， QoQ-31.24% ，預估稅後盈餘 0.42 億元，
YoY+238.86% ，QoQ-34.85% ，預估稅後 EPS 0.87 元。

三. 預估 2026 年稅後 EPS 4.00 元 
日成 KY 2026 年在主要客戶受到銀價上漲，新產品規劃以鉑金產
品為大宗 ， 其中日成KY 電鍍產能在經濟規模與品質良率受惠客戶
新產品訂單較大份額，將帶動營收成長；在獲利方面，在產品組
合優化與調整代工費帶動毛利率提升，進而帶動獲利成長。宏遠
預估日成 KY 2026 年營收金額 29.50 億元， YoY+38.62% ，預估
稅後盈餘 1.96 億元，由虧轉盈，預估稅後 EPS 4.00 元。

四. 預估 2027 年稅後 EPS 4.50 元 
日成 KY 2027 年在主要客戶新產品推出，刺激下游終端需求回
溫，進而推升主要客戶訂單維持高檔水準，其餘客戶方面，受惠
滲透率提升與拓展新地區業務，綜合上述，日成 2027 年營運維持
成長態勢。預估日成 KY 2027 年營收金額 32.00 億元，
YoY+8.48% ，預估稅後盈餘 2.20 億元， YoY+12.51% ，預估稅後
EPS 4.50 元。

貳、公 司 營 運 概 況

一.公司簡介 
日成控股成立於 1989 年，資本額 4.90 億元，並於 2017 年掛牌
上市，日成控股為流行珠寶及飾品設計製造出口企業，初期公司
名為日成有限公司。 1991 年公司更名為日成珠寶製造股份有限公
司，經過數年的經營，生產規模擴大，生產工藝及設計能力深受
國際客戶喜愛，並在當地珠寶及飾品設計製造產業享負盛名。有
鑑於公司成長及管理需求，積極推動專業管理方式，於 2003 獲得  
ISO 9001 認證。另，於 2004 年導入  ERP 系統，以因應公司未
來業務需求，快速成長趨勢，資源整合，以達有效管理及運用。
科技日新月異，日成公司為滿足客戶要求，不斷增強研發能力，
於 2007 年大量投入具有較強的設計能力及使用最先進的技術 ， 已
拓展生產能方面機器，如沖壓鑄造、金屬多樣鑄臺，並軟體以及
使用 3D 設計技術軟件等，設計出時尚與滿足客戶需求之產品。

圖一、日成控股身處產業中游地位

資料來源：公司、宏遠投顧整理

二. 2026 年營運概況及展望  
日成 -KY 主要營業項目為珠寶首飾設計、製造與銷售，產品包含
吊墜、戒指、耳環、手環、手鍊、項鍊與服飾配件等，主要生產
基地位於泰國曼谷近郊的龍仔厝，基地面積 6.59 萬平方米，員工
人數在 3100 人，滿載月產值在 3~3.5 億元。日成主要客戶多為國
際精品大廠，銷售區域遍布歐美亞三大洲，且日成控股泰國工廠
規模符合國際品牌代工條件，標準化生產製程具效率，且具有
ODM 設計開發能力。此外，公司也是泰國少數同時具有大規模產
能及電鍍產線的 ODM 代工廠。

圖二、珠寶產業分佈

資料來源：公司、宏遠投顧整理

觀察全球主要珠寶品牌商受到白銀價格大幅上漲侵蝕利潤與下游
終端客戶需求，因此將加速鉑金  (Platinum) 系列的轉型與推廣，
以多樣化產品線應對成本波動。為降低對白銀的依賴，計畫將部
分暢銷產品從銀製改為鍍鉑金設計，同時將產品線中銀製品的比
例從約 60% 降至 20% ，並希望在 2028 年前完成此轉型。由於鉑
金價格遠高於白銀，因此會在合金基底上鍍鉑金，既可減少鉑金
使用量，也有助控制成本，最終售價與銀製品相同，將有助廠商
降低銀價上漲侵蝕利潤的情況。

日成 KY 01~08/2026 營收金額 18.47 億元， YoY+39.00% 。日成
2026 年營運動能主要包括： 1，全球珠寶產業在 2022~2023 年經
歷後疫情時代庫存調整， 2024 年己有止穩並小幅回升情況， 2025
年在產業景氣持續回升，加上新材料實驗室鑽石價格也跌至甜蜜
點，品牌商將積極開發實驗室鑽石珠寶，有助整體產業 2026 年持
續回溫。 2，觀察第一大客戶 2021~2025 年營收占比，除 2023 年
占比 29% 較低外，其餘年度營收占比落在 43~52% ，在珠寶市場
己開始轉型鉑金產品，在電鍍加工的效率與良率將成為製程關
鍵，日成在電鍍品質與產能為泰國優秀廠商，預期在第一大客戶
在新產品推出帶動下， 2026 年營收將成長 35~40% 。3，在澳洲
區新客戶 (經營 3 年多 )與北美新客戶 (經營兩年多 )在多年來的深耕
經營與合作默契培養，預期 2026 年新客戶營收占比將有明顯提
升。預估日成 KY 2026 年營收金額 29.50 億元， YoY+38.62% 。

預期 2027 年，在原有客戶產品改款帶動下游需求熱絡，預期第一
大客戶 2027 年營收將小幅成長 5~10% ，其餘客戶方面，受惠滲
透率提升與新地區業務開拓帶動下 ， 預期2027 年營收成長幅度將
落在 15~20% 。綜合上述，預估日成 KY 2027 年營收金額 32.0 億
元， YoY+8.48% 。

研 究  報 告                
達明(4585.TT) 
產業：電子–其他電子 
協作機器人與 AI 實體化需求快速成⻑，享技術優勢與集團奧援 
 投資評價與建議 
業界唯⼀原⽣標配AI視覺，成⻑速度可望優於產業：達明扮演廣達集團(2382)
端側實體AI與工業自動化末端執行的關鍵戰略角色，隨著製造業由 「大規模標
準化」轉向「少樣多樣柔性⽣產」，協作機器⼈的需求快速成⻑，達明的產品
是業界唯⼀原⽣標配AI視覺，成⻑速度可望優於產業，惟目前評價已在上緣。 
 重點評論分析 
2Q26稅前淨利季增81%，2H營運優於1H： 2Q26營收5.1億元季增6%(年增
29%)，毛利率因高毛利率產品比重提升而由1Q26的49.9%增加至52.3%，營
業外收入中包含⼈形機器⼈專案的政府補助金約新台幣3,000萬元，稅前淨利
1.4億元季增81%，EPS 1.18元，1H26EPS 1.83元；客戶擴產、AI伺服器產能
建置、大負載搬運自動化需求帶動下，2H26營運優於1H26。 
半導體 、 伺服器及AI等產業具優勢 ， 高階產品逐步拉高將有助於毛利率的提升 ：
AI推升工業自動化的需求，達明將把握半導體、伺服器及AI等產業的趨勢及優
勢，機器⼈市場的年複合成⻑率約20％～30％，2026~2028年的營收成⻑率
均可優於產業平均；標準協作機器⼈手臂產品比重已降至50%以下，高階產品
如AI視覺與複合式機器⼈及⼈形機器⼈與實體AI比重將逐年拉高，將有助於毛
利率的提升。 
 投資風險 
差異化優勢減退、同業殺價競爭。

2Q26營益率提升至7.9%

資料來源 : CMoney 
營益率提升至52.3%，2Q26稅前淨利季增81%：2Q26營收5.1億元季增6%(年增29%)，毛利率因高毛利率產品比重提
升而由1Q26的49.9%增加至52.3% ， 營業利益率由1Q26的5.4%提升至7.9% ； 營業外收入中包含⼈形機器⼈專案的政府
補助金約新台幣3,000萬元 ， 補助期間約2年 ， 總補助金額大於1億元 ； 稅前淨利1.4億元季增81%(相較2Q25則由虧轉盈) ，
EPS 1.18元，1H26EPS 1.83元。 
客戶擴產、AI伺服器產能建置、大負載搬運自動化需求帶動下，2H26營運優於1H26：7月營收1.42億元年增24%，8月
營收1.53億元年減6%，前8月累計營收 12.9 億元年增10%；隨著主要客戶雲達赴美國籌設三座廠，以及⺟公司集團廣
達(2382)北美的智慧製造計畫推進，客戶擴產、AI伺服器產能建置、大負載搬運自動化需求帶動下，2H26營運可望優於
1H26，尤其是半導體及系統整合(從機器手臂、流水線、機台、料架到自走車⼀條龍整合)的訂單動能；AI協作機器⼈已
於1H26成功導入集團⺟公司廣達(2382)位於德國的車用電腦及車用電子產品製造工廠，雙方透過整合集團資源共同協
作，針對高複雜度的車載自動化光學檢測（AOI） 進行產線全面智慧化升級；先進駕駛輔助系統（ADAS） 所需的車用電
子控制單元屬於具備高度整合與強大運算能⼒之產品，單⼀主機板上的零組件數量高達近5,000顆，高密度車規電路設
計⽣產與製造流程亦高度複雜，藉由達明的AI協作機器⼈順利導入廣達位於德國的車載⽣產線，成功突破製造瓶頸並提
升整體⽣產效率；2026年推出45公斤級重負載機械手臂TM45S，並可透過雙臂協同作業，將整體負載能⼒提高至最高
